bugs.title: Job stops being tracked for lock renewal before the processor runs
bugs.description: processJob calls this.lockManager.untrackJob(job.id) immediately before callProcessJob. trackJob added the job a few lines earlier, so the job is removed from trackedJobs while its processor is still running. The lock extender timer only renews locks of tracked jobs, so this job's lock is never renewed.
bugs.runtime_failure: The lock taken when the job was fetched expires after lockDuration. The stalled-job checker then sees an active job without a lock, treats it as stalled and moves it back to wait. Another worker (or this one) fetches it and runs the processor again while the first run is still going: duplicate processing. When the first run finishes, its moveToCompleted/moveToFailed no longer owns the lock (in BullMQ this fails with 'Missing lock for job' or 'Lock mismatch'). After maxStalledCount stalls the job is failed as stalled.
bugs.conditions: Only when the processor runs longer than lockDuration (30 s by default), plus up to one stalledInterval. Shorter jobs complete before the lock expires, so tests and light traffic hide the bug.
bugs.fix: Delete the untrackJob call before callProcessJob. Untrack only once the job has finished: the completion and failure paths and the finally block already do that.

worsenings.title: Appending to the linked list walks the whole list
worsenings.description: LinkedList.push() finds the last node by walking from head every time, although the class keeps a tail pointer for exactly this. Each push is O(n) instead of O(1).
worsenings.when_it_matters: When the queue holds many items, e.g. with a high concurrency setting; at small sizes it is invisible.
worsenings.better: Append at the tail: this.tail.next = newNode, then this.tail = newNode.

rubric.point: A and B are fetched one after the other (each fetch is awaited before the next) and both start at about 0 s; the inner loop then stops fetching because numTotal() has reached 2.

C starts at about 1 s, when A finishes: handleCompleted calls moveToCompleted with fetchNext true, which returns the next job, so A's processJob resolves to C and mainLoop picks it up from the queue without a separate fetch.
All three are done at about 2 s; after that the fetches find nothing, the worker emits 'drained' and starts waiting for new jobs.

The inner loop only fetches while asyncFifoQueue.numTotal() < _concurrency; numTotal() is the pending promises (fetches and running processJob calls) plus resolved results not yet taken out, so two running jobs make it 2.

Fetching also stops while waiting for jobs, rate limited, closing or paused; and fetchNextCallback (numTotal() <= _concurrency) stops a finishing job from fetching another when the worker is already full.

A timer fires every 7.5 s (lockRenewTime / 2); on each tick it extends the locks of tracked jobs whose last renewal is more than 7.5 s old, so this job's lock is extended roughly every 7.5 to 15 s while it stays tracked.
If an extension fails, the worker emits 'lockRenewalFailed' and an 'error' for that job; nothing else stops, so the job keeps running even though its lock may run out.
On the first tick a job tracked with ts 0 only gets its ts set to now; once untrackJob() is called the job is no longer renewed at all.
untrackJob(job.id) is called right before callProcessJob, so the job is removed from tracking while the processor runs and its lock is never renewed.
Once the lock expires, the stalled checker moves the job back to wait and a worker runs it again while the first run continues: duplicate processing.
It only happens when the processor runs longer than lockDuration (30 s by default); short jobs hide it.
Fix: remove the early untrackJob; the completion/failure paths and finally already untrack once the job is done.
When the first run finishes it no longer holds the lock, so moving the job to completed/failed is rejected, and after maxStalledCount stalls the job fails as stalled.
Processors should be idempotent anyway: delivery is at-least-once, so a job can run twice even without this bug (for example when a worker crashes mid-job).

Each way out of processJob (unrecoverable failure, completion, error) untracks the job just before moving it out of active, so renewal stops once the job is finished; finally is a safety net for any path that throws or returns early.
untrackJob is a Map delete, so calling it more than once is harmless (idempotent).
They are not failures: the processor has deliberately moved the job to delayed, waiting or waiting-children, so the worker must not call moveToFailed (which would count a failed attempt).
Instead the worker just fetches its next job (moveToActive) if it may fetch; the rate-limit error is a third special case that moves the job back to wait and sets limitUntil.
push() walks from head to the last node on every call, so adding to a queue of n items costs O(n) and filling it costs O(n²).
It is pointless: the list already keeps a tail pointer (it even sets this.tail afterwards); append with this.tail.next = newNode, which is O(1).
It matters when many items are queued at once, for example a high concurrency setting; with concurrency 2 the list stays tiny, which is why it goes unnoticed.
Keep the job's lock renewed for the whole processor run (track it until it finishes), and set lockDuration comfortably above the renewal interval.

Make the processor idempotent (deduplication key, or check-and-set on side effects) so a second run is harmless; stop work via the abort signal when the lock is lost; or split long jobs into smaller ones.

grader_notes: A line comment on worker.ts around line 334 that explains the missing lock renewal earns R9 to R11 even if Q4 is left blank.
Q5 names untrackJob, which points at the bug's area; credit Q4 only for the mechanism (renewal stops, lock expires, job re-run), not for merely quoting the extra call.
